findings.message: Stages builds its Driver over an injected LLMEffect. LLMEffect._call (squatch/llmeffect.py) calls self._llm.call(req) with no on_event, and Driver.__init__ (squatch/driver.py:72) takes no event callback. LLMRequest carries ticket but not run_seq. The ticket forbids changing LLMEffect._call but fences neither llmeffect.py nor driver.py, and it never names the mechanism that routes on_event and run_seq to the detector. As written, 'bind at construction' plus a signal body with `run_seq` has no stated buildable path inside the fence.
findings.paved_road: Name the binding mechanism inside the fence. For example: a watchdog-owned LLM wrapper in squatch/watchdog.py that forwards on_event to CliClient.call, installed where compose builds the Stages LLMEffect, with Stages.run (fenced) supplying the per-run ticket/run_seq context. Otherwise fence squatch/driver.py and squatch/llmeffect.py and state the exact change allowed there.

findings.message: Scope in calls squatch/providers.py a 'fenced on-demand inspection exception', but it is not in the Scope fence. The binding also consumes the CliClient.call on_event seam that providers.py owns, so ownership needs the owner fenced or the exception claim removed.
findings.paved_road: Add squatch/providers.py to the Scope fence as an on-demand exception, keeping the Scope out prohibition on changing CliClient.call. Or remove it from the exception list and state that it is read-only preservation Context.

findings.message: Acceptance criteria 1 and 3 name 'the drain path' as a prover, but it is not a test file. tests/test_drain.py is not fenced, so the drain-dispatch reconciliation and drain-driver binding proofs have no named, fenced home.
findings.paved_road: Name tests/test_watchdog_activation.py as the file that proves bootstrap-drain binding and per-dispatch reconciliation. Or fence tests/test_drain.py as an on-demand exception and cite it explicitly.
